content_html_sanitized:
I had never had any particular opinion about psychiatry or psychology as medical science, until I got involved in the marijuana reform movement and met my late great friend, Harvard Medical School professor, Dr. Lester Grinspoon.

See Lester Grinspoon The Forbidden Professor RIP

 

My impression of him was definitely positive, although that may have been influenced by all the smoke in the air at NORML’s First People’s Pot Conference in 1972, where we met.

 

However, as the air cleared and my opinion of Lester grew, my opinion of psychiatry greatly diminished. As I described in his obituary above, twenty one years later, in 1993, Harvard Press would not print his book about medical marijuana, and the Harvard student newspaper, pointed out that he remained an Assistant Professor, despite the fact that he had founded The Harvard Mental Health newsletter.

 

Harvard medical school treated Lester very shabbily up until he died, but they treated his good friend and colleague, the late Norman Zinberg even worse.

 

Zinberg was a strong supporter of cannabis reform, but the Harvard University's Department of Psychiatry and Division of Addictions actually gave its annual achievement award, named for Norman Zinberg, to the Drug Czar, General, Clinton's drug czar.

There was outrage at such intellectual dishonesty.

See Harvard Medical School Gives General McCaffrey Zinberg Award

And

Documentation on McCaffrey’s Lies By Kevin Zeese

And

Bizarro to Leave after the First of the Year! Goes Out Lying.

 

Of course, we are expected to just forget about this absurdity, but here is a recent example of the misuse of the supposed expertise of a psychologist. Why Does Newsweek Push Prohibitionist Propaganda?

 

Psychology and psychiatry are not about economics or social policy, but clearly Harvard and other medical schools have politicized their supposed expertise and are harming the people they are supposed to help.
